questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to visit the US. The whether, nature and culture of California seemed great. From there I chose to go with Berkeley based on the academics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be ready to apply for a lot of grants - it is surprisingly expensive in and around Berkeley.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Realy easy - but I lived in the International House, which made it all very easy.
With regards to classes we got loads of information in the beginning of the semester - otherwise ask you fellow students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Digital information from UC Berkeley - due to covid it was online though, which wasn't great (and we still had to pay for it).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite hard actually - got my spot in International House (I-House) only 2 weeks prior to arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is expensive.
Further, I-House wants to decrease the number of 1-semester visitors living there, so it might be more difficult getting a spot unless you spend the entire academic year.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We had several application rounds for the courses - but some courses had massive waiting lists.
For some courses (most not in your major or grad-courses) you have to write the professor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't know - figured it out in the portal (Cal-central).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Did not get 1 of those I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it early - but don't panic. A lot of people drop classes in the first weeks of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 5 undergraduate courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More free writing and oral parts.
More discussion of what you think and way more articles (less theoretical than back home).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 135 The History of Economic Growth
ECON 191 Topics in Economic Research
POLSCI 179 Colloquium in Political Science
STAT 33A Introduction to Programming in R
UGBA 128 Strategic Cost Management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
POLSCI 179 Colloquium in Political Science is perfect if you need one more unit. It is a series of lectures from guest speakers (on e.g. Voluntary euthanasia, American politics, prison, climate, labor and wages) once a week and then a "for-fun" exam on your phone in the end of the semester. Extremely interesting but not a lot of work.

Topics were alright as well - not too much work and you get to experience the "best of ECON faculty".

questions.answer:
Travelling around was a bit more expensive than expected. 
Spend more on the bars than expected as well ;-).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing were very expensive.
(My housing of 13000 DKK a month in I-house were with food).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds - from every sport imagineable to a Harry Potter or block chain club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any - I think 1 semester were too short a stay for me to get involved.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Spend time in SF, to see the nature parks nearby (Yosemite, Tahoe etc.).
GO TO VEGAS on a weekend (nummer på en promoter som fik os gratis ind på et par vilde klubber +19125315148).
Kør route 1, men behøves ikke fortsætte efter Santa Barbera - LA er kedelig.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy in I-House - a lot of europeans.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dining hall in I-house - in general I think your housing is important - try the coops if you are ready for something a bit different.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind - maybe having a (young) roomate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sports and parties.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find good housing, go for the grants and don't choose to many hard courses. You will need time to adjust and socialize (and travel).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life in I-house - meeting new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: NO.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
